safeAccessPolicies.title: Safe Access Policies
safeAccessPolicies.intro: Each night, after the import, every Safe with accounts is checked against the first enabled policy (in order) whose Safe names match it. A Required rule needs a member whose name matches its pattern ({'{'}SafeName{'}'} is the Safe's own name, * is any text) holding a Safe role, and can ask for people in it (Vault group members or AD users). A Forbidden rule allows no member matching its pattern, or none holding the role it names. Progress Rules can then use "Safe access compliant" and "Compliance reviewed".

safeAccessPolicies.rolesIntro: A Safe role is a set of Safe permissions a member must hold. With "exactly", it must hold no others.

cyberArkSourcesEdit.title: CyberArk Sources
cyberArkSourcesEdit.intro: The nightly SQL Agent job imports these sources, then loads them. Privilege Cloud has no Run now; Self-Hosted has Pull now on Data Sources. Changes apply from the next nightly run.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.notConfigured: Not set up yet: the nightly import fails until these settings are saved. Re-running the installer's nightly job step also saves them.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.exportFolderHint: SQL Server's service account reads the files, so it needs read access to this folder.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.dateTokenHint: {'{'}yyyy-MM-dd{'}'} (or another date format in braces) is replaced with the run's date. Wildcards aren't allowed.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.directIntro: BlueTrack reads Safes, accounts, Safe members, users, groups and platforms from PVWA each night, before the import job, using the credential below. It sees only what that account can see (its Safe memberships), so a pull whose Safe or account count changes by more than the allowed percentage is rejected and the nightly import fails until an admin accepts it. Pending (discovered) accounts are not read. Needs PAM Self-Hosted 14.2 or later.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.pvwaAddressHint: https only. The /PasswordVault part is optional.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.includeBuiltInSafesHint: Also reads the Vault's internal Safes (such as PasswordManager_Accounts and PVWAConfig) and their members, which PVWA's Safe list leaves out. They show as CyberArk internal Safes. Off by default; turn it on to review whether that data is useful. The first pull after turning it on counts more Safes, which Allowed change may need to accept.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.pvwaFallbackHint: One per line, up to 5. Each pull and Test signs in to the PVWA address first; when it can't be reached (no connection, no answer, or 502/503/504), the next address is tried. A refused credential is never tried elsewhere.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.credentialHint: A named credential from Admin > Credentials. A CyberArk CP or CCP credential is fetched from the Vault at each pull. The account needs List Accounts and View Safe Members in the Safes to read, and the Audit Users Vault authorization; membership of the Auditors group lets it read CPM activity, and of Vault Admins, platform details.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.pullTimeHint: HH:mm, server time, every night. It must come before the nightly import job's time: the import fails if the latest pull is more than 20 hours old or didn't succeed.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.timeLimitHint: A pull, nightly or Pull now, still running after this long is stopped and logged as failed; the data the nightly load reads is left as it was. The first pull also reads every account's device type and linked accounts, one call each (later pulls only the changed ones), so a large Vault may need more time or a few nights. 5 to 720; the default is 45.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.detailRefreshLabel: Also re-read account details that haven't changed
cyberArkSourcesEdit.detailRefreshHint: Each pull reads an account's folder, device type and linked accounts again only when CyberArk says its properties changed. Moving an account to another folder may not count as a change, so this re-reads accounts read long enough ago, the oldest first.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.detailRefreshMaxHint: One PVWA call per account, 8 at a time; they count against the pull time limit. 1 to 100,000; the default is 1,000.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.maxChangeHint: The most the number of Safes or of accounts may change from the last good pull before a pull is rejected. A change of 5 or fewer is always allowed.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.restoredDraft: What you had typed here before leaving this page was restored. Nothing is saved until you press Save.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.createCredentialHint: Opens Admin > Credentials, then returns here with it chosen. What you've typed here is kept.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.plannedSources: Privilege Cloud Direct (reading Privilege Cloud through its API instead of the export folder) is planned, and not available yet.
cyberArkSourcesEdit.testFilesHint: Files were checked as the application pool's account sees them; SQL Server reads them as its own service account.

dataSources.pullStartedMessage: Pull started. When it succeeds, the Import and Load job runs. This page refreshes until both have finished.
dataSources.loadNotStarted: The Import and Load job couldn't be started, so the accounts change at the next nightly job: {message}
dataSources.loadUnknown: The Import and Load job didn't report back. Check its history in SQL Server Agent.
dataSources.confirmCancelPull: Stop the pull that is running? It will be logged as failed, and the data the nightly load reads is left as it was.
dataSources.cancelRequested: Cancelling the pull. The log shows it once it has stopped.
dataSources.confirmPull: It is business hours. Pull from PVWA now? It replaces the staged Self-Hosted data, and then the Import and Load job runs.
dataSources.confirmAcceptPull: The last pull was rejected because the Safe or account count changed more than allowed. Pull again and accept whatever PVWA returns? Accounts it no longer returns are marked deleted by the Import and Load that follows.
dataSources.bannerRejected: The latest pull was rejected, so tonight's import will fail until a pull succeeds. Open Details to see what changed.
dataSources.bannerFailed: The latest pull failed, so tonight's import will fail until a pull succeeds. Open Details to see why.
dataSources.pullDetailsAccepted: An admin accepted a change over the allowed percentage.
dataSources.pullMeaningSucceeded: The pull finished and replaced the staged Self-Hosted data. The next nightly import uses it. Any messages below are warnings: something was skipped or couldn't be read, and nothing else was affected.
dataSources.pullMeaningRejected: The pull read PVWA but wasn't used: the number of Safes or accounts changed by more than the allowed percentage from the last good pull. The staged data is unchanged, and the nightly import fails until a pull succeeds.
dataSources.pullMeaningFailed: The pull didn't finish. The staged data is unchanged, and the nightly import fails until a pull succeeds.
dataSources.pullMeaningStarted: The pull is still running, or stopped without finishing (the application restarted). The next pull marks it failed.
dataSources.pullAdviceRejected: If the change is expected, such as Safes that were deleted, use Accept the change and pull. If it isn't, check that the service user is still a member of the Safes it should see (List Accounts and View Safe Members), then pull again.
dataSources.pullAdviceFailed: Check the message above. Common causes: the credential was refused or its CP/CCP lookup failed (test it on Admin > Credentials), PVWA can't be reached from this server, or the PVWA address is wrong. Then use Pull now.
dataSources.dataFeedsIntro: Data feeds import a CSV file from a folder, using the same imports as the Bulk Actions uploads. Enabled feeds run every night, in the order shown; the newest file matching the pattern is imported and left in place. The application pool's account needs read access to each folder.

runProgress.cannotSeeSessions: What its SQL Server session is waiting on isn't shown: the installer's Db.SessionActivity step hasn't signed the procedure that reads it (that needs a SQL Server administrator).
runProgress.sessionEnded: Its SQL Server session ({session}) has ended, so this run will never finish: it was stopped, or SQL Server restarted.
runProgress.blockerState: That session is {status} with {transactions} open transaction(s), running {command}; its last request started {since}.
runProgress.step_AdGroups: AD members of the Safe groups
runProgress.stallHelp: A pull that reads nothing, or a Load procedure, Import or Snapshot still running, for this long is stalled: the Run stalled email (Notifications) and the Pull and Load check on the Deployment page report it. 5 to 1,440 minutes.
runProgress.confirmCancel: Stop the Import and Load SQL Agent job? The Load is rolled back, so the data stays as it was before it started, and the run is logged as failed. Tonight's job runs as usual.
runProgress.cancelDone: The job was stopped. SQL Server may take a moment to roll the Load back.
runProgress.cancelRefused: SQL Server Agent didn't stop the job: {reason}
runProgress.noFiles: No export files were imported: Privilege Cloud isn't imported from files, or the run stopped before its first file.

globalApplicationConfiguration.scheduledBackupRetentionHint: After each scheduled backup, older scheduled backup files are deleted. Backups made with "Backup App" are never deleted.

globalApplicationConfiguration.exportMaxRowsHint: The most rows one report export (Export CSV / Export Excel) may hold, from 1 to 1,000,000. When more rows match, the export is refused with the count instead of being cut short (D-220).
globalApplicationConfiguration.patternHelpRegex: {try} on sample names (one per line). {prefix} matches the start of the name, {suffix} the end; both ignore case. {regex} is a regular expression, also ignoring case. Example: {example} matches {match1}, {match2} and {match3}, but not {nonMatch1} or {nonMatch2}.
globalApplicationConfiguration.patternHelpNoRegex: {try} on sample names (one per line). {prefix} matches the start of the name, {suffix} the end; both ignore case. {regex} needs SQL Server 2025, so it isn't available on this server.
globalApplicationConfiguration.nightlyRunTimeHint: Server local time. Default 04:00, after the 02:00 Import and Load job.
globalApplicationConfiguration.businessDaysHint: Run now asks for confirmation inside these hours, since an import changes data people are working with.
globalApplicationConfiguration.apiKeyLifetimeHint: How long a new API key lasts before it expires, from 1 to 365. The expiry can be changed for each key when it is created.
globalApplicationConfiguration.apiRateLimitLabel: API requests per minute, per key:
globalApplicationConfiguration.apiRateLimitHint: The most requests one API key may make in a minute, from 1 to 100,000. Over it, the API answers "too many requests" until the minute is up.
globalApplicationConfiguration.apiKeyReminderLabel: API key expiry reminder lead time (days):
globalApplicationConfiguration.apiKeyReminderHint: How many days before an API key expires its owner is emailed, from 1 to 90. The owner is emailed again on the day it expires, and the administrators on that day (the ApiKeyExpiring and ApiKeyExpired notification types on Notifications).
globalApplicationConfiguration.apiKeyRetentionHint: How many days an expired API key stays on the API Keys list before it is deleted automatically, from 1 to 3,650 (365 by default). 0 keeps them for ever. A key that is only disabled is never deleted automatically. Each deletion is in the Audit Log.

secretsStoreConfiguration.activateWarning: If {name} isn't set up correctly or can't be reached, those lookups fail until you make another backend active.
secretsStoreConfiguration.testIntro: Attempts a real retrieval against the active backend. Never shows the retrieved secret -- only whether it succeeded and non-secret metadata (username/address).
secretsStoreConfiguration.dpapiHint: WindowsDpapi is a local, flat store -- enter a {link} page credential's name as Object; Safe/Folder are ignored.

targetMatchReview.title: Target Match Review
targetMatchReview.intro: A weak match (e.g. an IP address alone, which can be reassigned by DHCP/NAT) found during import -- confirm rather than auto-merge.
targetMatchReview.linkHint: Link keeps the imported row as its own target, linked to the candidate (or to another target: search for it by name or by any identifier, at least 2 characters). The IP address stays where it is, and the linked pair counts once, at the risk score of the target it's linked to. New Target keeps it as a separate target. Ignore also skips this row in later imports.
targetMatchReview.notStored: Not stored (queued before this version). Name:
targetMatchReview.ignoreWarning: Ignoring is remembered: this row won't be offered for review again.
targetMatchReview.newTargetNotice: A new target was created for {identifier}.
targetMatchReview.ignoredNotice: {identifier} was ignored, and won't be offered for review again.

notifications.testNeedsSave: The test uses the saved SMTP settings. Save your changes first.
notifications.confirmDelete: Delete recipient "{email}"? This cannot be undone.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: SMTP settings, the recipient list and the schedule for BlueTrack's automated alerts (e.g. a failed nightly Import and Load, overdue Risk Exceptions, the weekly summary).
notifications.helpMicrosoft365: App-only sign-in to Exchange Online: server smtp.office365.com, port 587, STARTTLS. The app needs the SMTP.SendAsApp permission with admin consent, a service principal registered in Exchange Online with access to the mailbox, and SMTP AUTH turned on for the mailbox.
notifications.helpGoogle: A service account with domain-wide delegation for https://mail.google.com/ signs in as the mailbox: server smtp.gmail.com, port 587, STARTTLS. Store the service account's whole JSON key file as the credential's password.
notifications.helpGeneric: A client credentials token from your OAuth2 provider, sent to the SMTP server as XOAUTH2. The token URL must use https.
notifications.ignoreCrl: Ignore CRL issues (skip certificate revocation checking)
notifications.ignoreSsl: Ignore all SSL errors (skip all certificate validation -- use with caution)
notifications.typesIntro: Turn each alert kind on or off, and optionally pick a target role -- additive to the recipient list below: the role's own email plus, if LDAP is configured, every member of its mapped AD groups.
notifications.scheduleIntro: When the scheduled emails go out, in the server's local time. Each goes out once: the daily digest once a day, the weekly summary once a week.
notifications.ownerIntro: With OverdueRiskExceptions on, each application's owner (its Owner Email on Admin > Application ↔ Safe Mapping) also gets a daily email, at the daily digest time, of the Active exceptions on their applications that are overdue for review.
notifications.ownerIncludeAccountExceptions: Also list exceptions on single accounts that belong to the application
notifications.ownerReminderDays: Also remind the owner this many days before the review date (0 = no reminder):
notifications.testIntro: Sends a real test email to every active recipient below, using the saved SMTP configuration.
notifications.noRecipients: No recipients configured yet -- alerts have nowhere to go until at least one is added below.

riskScoreBands.emptyNone: No risk score bands are defined yet.

riskScoreBands.title: Bands
riskScoreBands.intro: Named ranges over the computed risk score (0-1000) -- e.g. Low/Medium/High/Critical. The resulting band name shows up on the Account Progress list and the Risk Score report. A new/edited range must not overlap any other existing band.

rolesAndPermissions.confirmDelete: Delete role "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
rolesAndPermissions.deleteFailedInUse: Delete failed: {status} (a role still mapped to a group can't be deleted)
rolesAndPermissions.title: Roles & Permissions

accountClassification.title: Account Classification
accountClassification.seeDiscovered: See the result on Discovered Accounts
accountClassification.intro: Separates a person's day-to-day (Primary) account from their Secondary and Admin accounts on Reports > Discovered Accounts, and finds each account's Owner (the person's primary account). Attribute rules are checked first, then Name rules, then OU rules, each in the order shown; the first enabled rule that matches sets the class. Saving anything here reclassifies every discovered account at once, from what the last discovery run read -- no directory lookup.
accountClassification.ownerByEmployeeId: Find the owner by a shared employee ID
accountClassification.settingsHint: The owner by employee ID is the one enabled account in the same domain sharing the ID whose class is Primary (or, for a Secondary/Admin account, the one that matches no rule); if more than one could be, the owner is left empty as ambiguous. Turning classification on makes the next discovery run read the attributes the rules need.
accountClassification.attributeRulesIntro: Checked first. An Active Directory attribute from a fixed list (adminCount, employeeType, extensionAttribute1-15, description, title, department) equals, contains, starts with or is set -- for example adminCount equals 1 is Admin.
accountClassification.nameRulesIntro: A prefix, suffix or wildcard pattern (* any text, ? one character) on sAMAccountName or userPrincipalName. A Secondary or Admin rule on sAMAccountName also gives the owner: the name without the prefix or suffix (adm.jsmith is owned by jsmith), or the text a pattern's single * matched.
accountClassification.ouRulesIntro: The account's distinguished name contains or ends with an OU path, for example OU=Admin Accounts,DC=corp,DC=example.
accountClassification.confirmDelete: Delete the rule "{rule}"? Every discovered account is reclassified without it.

accountClassificationRuleEdit.notFound: Rule not found -- it may have been deleted.
accountClassificationRuleEdit.hintAttribute: Only the listed attributes can be used. "Is set" matches any value.
accountClassificationRuleEdit.hintName: Starts with is a prefix (adm.), ends with a suffix (-a); a pattern uses * for any text and ? for one character (a?-*). A Secondary or Admin rule on sAMAccountName also gives the owner.
accountClassificationRuleEdit.hintOu: Part of the distinguished name, for example OU=Admin Accounts,DC=corp,DC=example. Case and spaces after commas are ignored.

siemForwarding.title: SIEM Forwarding
siemForwarding.intro: Sends every new audit log event to your SIEM as a CEF (Common Event Format) message inside RFC 5424 syslog, over TCP or TLS, within a few seconds of it being written. Events wait in the database while the collector can't be reached and are sent when it comes back, oldest first; the audit purge keeps any event not yet sent. Turning forwarding on starts with the events written from then on: older events aren't sent.
siemForwarding.enabled: Forward the audit log to the SIEM
siemForwarding.enabledHint: Use Test first: it sends one test event with the saved settings, whether forwarding is on or off.
siemForwarding.framingHint: Octet counting puts each message's length in front of it; it is the framing RFC 5425 specifies for TLS and the default. Choose line feed only if your collector needs it. The default port is 6514 for TLS and 514 for TCP.
siemForwarding.tlsHint: The trust store and CA options also check that the certificate names the host above. A pinned fingerprint trusts exactly that certificate (for a self-signed collector), so update it when the collector's certificate changes. There is no option to ignore certificate errors.
siemForwarding.syslogHostName: Syslog host name (blank: this server's name)
siemForwarding.messageHint: Each event is sent as a CEF message with vendor and product BlueTrack and version {version}; its signature ID is the event type and its name the event type's description. It carries the event's time, user, source address, entity, detail, reason, field changes and audit event number. A message over the size limit loses its field-change summary first, then has its detail shortened.
siemForwarding.eventTypesHint: Choose which audit events are forwarded and the CEF severity each is sent with (0-10: 0-3 low, 4-6 medium, 7-8 high, 9-10 very high). Read/view events only exist when Log read/view events is on in Global Application Configuration.
siemForwarding.testHint: Saves nothing. The test event is recorded in the audit log as a ConnectionTest.

apiKeys.title: API Keys
apiKeys.intro: API keys let scripts and other systems call the API without a person signing in. A script sends its key to {endpoint} and gets a token that lasts 10 minutes, then calls the API with that token, acting as the key's role. A key can never hold the permissions that manage API keys, sign-in, roles, secrets or settings.
apiKeys.noKeys: There are no API keys yet.
apiKeys.confirmDelete: Delete the API key "{name}"? Scripts that use it stop working at once.
apiKeys.rotateConfirm: Rotate the API key "{name}"? A new key with the same role is created and shown once. The old key keeps working until you disable or delete it.
apiKeys.rotatedHeading: A new API key "{name}" was created from "{from}".
apiKeys.rotateHint: Rotate creates a new key with the same role, for switching a caller over. The old key keeps working until you disable or delete it.

apiKeyCreate.title: New API Key
apiKeyCreate.nameHint: What the key is for, for example the script or system that uses it.
apiKeyCreate.roleHint: What the key may do is what this role may do. The Admin role is not offered, and a key never gets the permissions that manage API keys, sign-in, roles, secrets or settings.
apiKeyCreate.lifetimeHint: Up to {max} days. The default is set on Global Application Configuration.
apiKeyCreate.copyWarning: Copy the key now. It is shown only once and can't be shown again; if it is lost, delete the key and create a new one.
apiKeyCreate.leaveWarning: The key is shown only once. After you leave this page it can't be shown again.
apiKeyCreate.copyFailed: Could not copy automatically. Select the key above and copy it by hand.
apiKeyCreate.ownerHint: Who is emailed before the key expires, and on the day it does. Leave it blank to tell only the administrators.
apiKeyCreate.rateLimitHint: This key's own limit. Leave it blank to use the limit on Global Application Configuration.

apiClientMappings.title: API client mappings
apiClientMappings.intro: A script can also sign in with a token from your identity provider instead of an API key. It sends that token to the same address and gets an API token that lasts 10 minutes. The role it gets comes from the first mapping that matches its token, lowest order first: by the token's client (a script's own application), or by a value in its groups claim (the claim named on the identity provider). Only roles you list here are given, never Admin. These mappings are separate from Group → Role Mapping, which is for people signing in.
apiClientMappings.noMappings: There are no API client mappings yet.
apiClientMappings.noProviders: Mappings need an enabled OIDC identity provider. Set one up under Identity Providers first.
apiClientMappings.confirmDelete: Delete the mapping for {what}? Callers who relied on it are refused, and tokens it already gave stop working within a minute.
apiClientMappings.matchHint: Client: the token's client ID (its azp or client_id claim). Group: a value in the token's groups claim.
apiClientMappings.orderHint: When more than one mapping matches a token, the lowest order is used.

apiKeyEdit.title: Edit API Key
apiKeyEdit.notFound: That API key no longer exists.
apiKeyEdit.roleHint: A role change applies at once, including to tokens the key has already been given.
apiKeyEdit.expiredNote: This key expired on {date}. Saving without choosing a new date leaves its expiry as it is.
apiKeyEdit.expiresHint: The last day the key works (up to {max} days from today). Change it to renew the key or to shorten it; to stop a key now, disable or delete it.

platformMapping.saveNeedsType: Choose an account type to save.
platformMapping.title: Platform Mapping
platformMapping.intro: Each CyberArk platform (Privilege Cloud's own list; for Self-Hosted, one platform per policy ID) can be given the account type and source of record its accounts start with. A new account gets them when BlueTrack first tracks it, and both can still be changed on each account. Platforms with no mapping are listed first.
platformMapping.fillExisting: When saving, also fill accounts already tracked on the platform that have no account type or source of record
platformMapping.fillHint: An account that already has an account type or source of record is never changed.
platformMapping.savedFilled: Saved the mapping of {platform}: filled {types} account(s) with no account type and {sors} with no source of record.
platformMapping.removed: Removed the mapping of {platform}. Accounts keep what they have.
platformMapping.confirmRemove: Remove the mapping of {platform}? Accounts already given an account type keep it; new accounts on this platform get none by default.
platformMapping.useAllSuggestions: Fill in {count} suggestion | Fill in {count} suggestions
platformMapping.suggestionsHint: Fills the drop-downs of the platforms shown that have a suggestion and no account type chosen. Nothing is saved until you click Save on each row; group platforms get no suggestion.

progressRules.title: Progress Rules
progressRules.intro: Each night, after the import, an account moves from a rule's From stage to its To stage when all of the rule's conditions match it. Accounts only move forward, can move through several stages in one night, and are never moved while Risk Accepted / Excluded or Archived; their status is kept. An archive rule instead sets matching accounts at any stage to Archived (out of scope, counted on its own); the archive rules run first. Archived stays until someone changes the status, and an account someone took out of Archived isn't archived again until the archive rules have stopped matching it. Change the stages themselves on Blueprint Stages.
progressRules.confirmDelete: Delete the rule "{name}"? Accounts it already moved stay where they are.
progressRules.empty: No rules: accounts change stage only when someone edits them.

field.cpmDisabledReason: Why the CPM doesn't manage it

progressRuleEdit.name: Name
progressRuleEdit.actionMove: Moves accounts to a later stage
progressRuleEdit.conditionsHint: Text compares without regard to case. "Is one of" takes a comma-separated list. "Not" conditions also match an empty value. At least one condition.
progressRuleEdit.sourceHint: PRIVCLOUD, SELFHOSTED, DISCOVERY, or a data feed's source code.
progressRuleEdit.previewCount: {count} account at the From stage would move now. | {count} accounts at the From stage would move now (up to 50 are listed).
progressRuleEdit.previewArchiveCount: {count} account would be archived now. | {count} accounts would be archived now (up to 50 are listed).
progressRuleEdit.folderHint: Root is the top of the Safe; read from PVWA's account details (Self-Hosted Direct).
progressRuleEdit.cpmDisabledReasonHint: The reason given when automatic management was turned off, for example ADArchive.

blueprintStages.title: Blueprint Stages
blueprintStages.intro: The stages an account goes through, in order. New accounts start at the stage marked Start. Each KPI (Onboarded, Managed, Compliant) counts the accounts at its milestone's stage or later, so the milestones must stay in that order. A stage can be deleted only when no account, rule or history uses it.

riskScoreDefaults.intro: The scores BlueTrack starts with, and how much each kind of finding adds to the risk score of the accounts it affects. Scores are 0 to 1,000.
riskScoreDefaults.addressTarget: Target made from an account's address
riskScoreDefaults.addressTargetHelp: The nightly load makes a target for each account address that has none, with this score. Targets made before keep theirs.
riskScoreDefaults.newHelp: The score a new target or access group starts with on its Add form.
riskScoreDefaults.findingsIntro: A finding counts like a target the account reaches, with this risk value, in the active risk algorithm: a hard-coded secret found on a system counts for every account that reaches that target, and for the account it names. Changing a value marks every score to recalculate: use Recalculate Now on Reports > Risk Score, or wait for the nightly load.
riskScoreDefaults.savedRescore: Saved. Every score is marked to recalculate: use Recalculate Now on Reports > Risk Score, or wait for the nightly load.

riskFindings.intro: What raises risk scores now, from the latest DNA import: each hard-coded secret on the system it was found on and on the account it names, and Pass-the-Hash and non-compliant DNA accounts on the BlueTrack account they are linked to. Rows is how many DNA rows gave the finding.
riskFindings.refreshed: Findings refreshed. Scores change at the next recalculation.
riskFindings.emptyNone: No findings. Import DNA on Admin > Data Sources to find hard-coded secrets and risky accounts.
